title: Entrained release controller with revert playbooks and telemetry gates
author: Asha Kulkarni
release_notes: Introduce an "entrained" release controller that progressively promotes model variants based on session-level telemetry convergence. Adds packaged revert playbooks and a telemetry-gate library. No user-facing API breaking changes; operator-visible knobs added.
description:
Context and motivation: We need a rollout primitive that can safely promote model variants in environments where session continuity and multi-signal coherence matter (e.g., chat sessions that span multiple requests). Existing canary controllers in the repo operate purely on aggregate metrics and time-based ramps, which can cause noisy signals and false positives when per-session drift occurs. This PR implements an "entrained" release controller: a promotion engine that requires telemetry signals to 'entrain' (converge) across a configurable number of sessions before increasing traffic fraction. The controller is intended for model lifecycle flows (A/B tests, staggered promotions, and experimental lanes) where session-level fidelity reduces flakiness when deciding to promote or revert.

What this PR delivers (high level):
- A new controller component (controller/entrained) that coordinates staged promotion based on session-coalesced telemetry gates and time windows.
- A small domain-specific playbook format (pkg/playbook/revert_playbook.yaml + ops/playbooks examples) that encodes stepwise revert steps and human-check hooks.
- A telemetry gate library (pkg/telemetry/gates) that provides common gate types: session-stability, percentile-stationarity, and cross-signal decorrelation checks.
- Durable decision logs and a compact audit record (operationally searchable) that capture why a promotion advanced or a revert was triggered.
- API surface: new fields on rollout CRD (entrainment_window_ms, min_sessions, gate_config_reference) and a backward-compatible admission path so older clients won't be broken.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The entrainment model requires maintaining short-lived session aggregates in-memory. To avoid O(N) blowup we keep a sliding window with cardinality caps and a low-memory probabilistic sampler when limits are reached. This favors conservative decisions under high cardinality rather than returning a false positive. The telemetry gates are pluggable so future gates (e.g., semantic drift) can be added without changing the controller core.

Files changed (high level):
- controller/entrained/controller.go (new): core promotion loop, leader election, decision logging
- api/v1alpha/rollout_types.go (modified): added entrainment_window_ms, min_sessions, gate_config_ref
- pkg/telemetry/gates/*.go (new): gate implementations and tests
- pkg/playbook/revert_playbook.yaml (new): playbook schema and sample playbooks in ops/

Review conversation (abridged):
- Drew Hamilton (review): "Nice ergonomics. Two concerns: (1) the cardinality cap behavior should be explicit in the docs and visible in console, (2) the probabilistic sampler introduces non-determinism which might complicate reproductions. Can we add an option to export the sampled keys so we can replay?"
- Asha (author): "Responded: added sampling export under debug=true and documented the cap behavior. The default remains conservative; replay artifacts are rotated daily and kept for 7 days."
- Sofia Ramirez (review): "Gate configs look good. Suggest tightening the default stationarity window to 60s for short-lived sessions — otherwise tests may take long locally."
- Asha: "Agreed — default now 60s, operator can extend via gate_config_reference. Updated tests to override defaults."
- Kenji Tanaka (approval): "Verified E2E stable on my cluster; telemetry logs show correct entrainment decision points. Approved."

CI and checks: Initial CI run (11/14) surfaced a flake in e2e (timeout under heavy load). I added a more deterministic telemetry mock and retried. Final CI summary:
- unit: pass
- integration: pass
- e2e: pass (after retry with mock server)
- lint: pass
- go vet: pass
- ui tests: pass
All checks green on merge.

Operational notes for SRE/Oncall: The controller emits a set of new metrics (rollout_entrainment_sessions_count, rollout_gate_breakdowns, rollout_decision_actions). Dashboards will be added in a follow-up but temporary panels are available under /dashboards/entrained. The revert playbooks are stored under ops/playbooks; operators may add org-specific playbooks. Decision logs are searchable via internal telemetry; a query example is included in ops/playbooks/entrained-release.md.

Backward compatibility: The CRD mutation path accepts missing entrainment fields and defaults to legacy time-based promotion behavior. Operators must opt-in to entrainment via the new fields or console toggle.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge after CI green and three approvals. Changelog entry included under docs/changelog/2024-11-21.md.

Follow-ups planned (separate PRs):
- Hooking up long-term dashboards and alert burn-down strategies (ENG-2399)
- Add semantic-drift gate and language-model-specific detectors (ENG-2418)
- Expose sampling replay UI in console for debugging (PM-1275)

Notes for reviewers/users: This PR is intended for operators who want tighter, session-aware promotions. It is not a replacement for our aggregate-metric rollouts in all cases; use entrained releases when session coherence matters (chat, multi-request pipelines, session-bound KV caches).
